observations: All 18 preset–seed–embedding analyses completed from the nine saved user files (PCA and FA), producing 288 combination rows, 1,152 day-stratified rows, 72 source-addition diagnostics, and 36 exact-independence diagnostics.

Default/PCA/raw scVelo velocity agreement on moving truth axes was 0.1338, 0.1770, and 0.2389 across seeds 0–2, below the 0.75 gate, although its oriented fraction was 0.7656, 0.7502, and 0.7119 and passed the 0.30 gate.

For default/PCA/raw flow conflicts, the instantaneous-flow truth sided with higher-ranked labelling in 0.9786, 0.9723, and 0.9691 of conflict pairs; combined flow coverage was non-decreasing and labelling decisions were unchanged exactly.

Default/PCA/raw lineage agreement on moving developmental-truth axes was 0.9953, 0.9879, and 0.9883 and passed the 0.95 gate. Combined developmental coverage was 0.8401, 0.8456, and 0.7979, below 0.90; in lineage–pseudotime conflicts the developmental truth sided with lineage in 0.9057, 0.6552, and 0.7164, below the 0.80 minimum for two seeds.
All source-addition coverage and higher-source-decision invariants held; flow/developmental outputs were exactly independent in every call and every stored S02 J hash remained unchanged.
The stationary-cycle flags are recorded in diagnostics: all calls identify non-equilibrium and non-stationarity fractions, with no equilibrium fraction observed.

suggestions: If issued as a separate task, investigate why the dynamical RNA-velocity readout retains broad orientation coverage but has weak agreement with the expected instantaneous-flow truth, stratified by sampling day and axes; this could distinguish a readout-calibration issue from biology-like transient state changes.
